title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: The server outside VS Code, repaired
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.42.32 repairs the standalone language server that Neovim, Helix and Zed talk to. Its index was frozen at startup, it could index your home directory instead of your project, and Go to Definition answered with every class of that name in the workspace. The permission hover also stops missing `SET_ALARM`.

highlights.title: The index follows your edits
highlights.description: The server now asks for save notifications and watches the files, so a deleted or renamed class no longer survives until the next restart.

highlights.title: Your project, not your home
highlights.description: `workspaceFolders` is honoured, every root is indexed, and no announced root means nothing is scanned instead of falling back to the working directory.

highlights.title: One definition, the imported one
highlights.description: Three same named classes no longer all show up: the file's imports decide, then its own package.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: The language server asks for save notifications and registers a file watcher, so deletions and renames reach the index.
`workspaceFolders` and multiple roots are honoured; nothing falls back to the process working directory.
Go to Definition narrows same named classes by explicit import, then wildcard import, then the file's own package.
References read open buffers instead of the disk copy, and `includeDeclaration: false` is honoured.
A README no longer becomes symbols, a symlink no longer walks the scan out of the project, and the permission hover finds `com.android.alarm.permission.SET_ALARM`.
